absorption: Each relevant data invariant is permanently enforced and no maintained environment needs the corresponding historical repair.

consumers.name: Explicit operator-driven repair of historical Honcho data.

contract: Reviewed opt-in SQL repairs can merge historical peer aliases and canonicalize legacy peer-card/display/memory text without being run automatically during service startup or fork upgrades.

fork: restore a disposable database snapshot, capture preflight counts, run exactly one reviewed repair, inspect post-state/invariants, then discard the database.
proof.fork_expected: rehearsed scripts converge the intended historical records without being part of automatic startup/migration execution.
upstream: inspect identity/data repair tooling on the recorded upstream base.
proof.upstream_expected: these local historical repair operations are absent.

replay: The scripts own their transactions; treat every real invocation as destructive and require a verified backup plus disposable rehearsal.
upstream_gap: The recorded upstream base has no repair scripts for these local historical identity/data invariants.
